subject: AWS Marketplace private offer — buyer approvals & term structure for Brookline AI
messages:
From: Jason Lewis <jason.lewis@brookline.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>; Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AWS Marketplace private offer — term length and approval path for Brookline AI

Hi Olga / Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this — we’re interested in moving forward with Redwood via an AWS Marketplace private offer. A few items procurement wants clarified before we start the private-offer flow:  

- Term vs. pricing: Our CFO prefers a 24-month commitment to lock pricing, but our product teams want flexibility for usage spikes. Can you share the delta in unit pricing between 12- and 24-month MPOs (both annual commit and usage-based with commit)?  
- Buyer approvals: Brookline has a two-tier approval (BU head + centralized procurement). Will that complicate the MPO signature window? Any recommendations to avoid multi-signer delays?  
- PO template: attaching our PO template (see Brookline_PO_Template.pdf). We prefer a single-signer MPO from procurement if possible; otherwise we need guidance on sequencing.

Goal is to have a clean MPO and DocuSign within two weeks if terms look reasonable.

Appreciate a quick note on the recommended path and any materials you need from me.

—Jason
Head of Procurement, Brookline AI

[Attachment: Brookline_PO_Template.pdf]

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Jason Lewis <jason.lewis@brookline.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 11:03:21 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace private offer — term length and approval path for Brookline AI

Jason — thanks, this is straightforward to solve. Short answer: we can support either path, but there are tradeoffs. Below is a concise recommendation and next steps.

Recommendation (what usually closes fastest):
- Offer: 12-month MPO with an option to extend a second 12-month term at a pre-agreed discount level (extension exercised by procurement in month 10).
- Pricing: ~7–12% additional discount for a firm 24-month up-front commit vs. 12-month. For usage-based with an annual minimum commit, the difference is smaller (4–6%). I’ll include a pricing band in the MPO draft.
- Approvals: To avoid blocking signatures across multiple BU heads, we recommend Brookline designate procurement as the MPO signer with an internal approval memo (procurement acceptance letter) rather than multiple signatures on the MPO itself. This keeps the AWS PO flow to a single signer.

What I need from you:
- Confirmation that procurement can sign on behalf of the company (we can reference an internal PO attachment).
- Any specific compliance clauses your legal/procurement require in the MPO (data residency, audit frequency).

I’ve attached an MPO draft with two term options and a sample extension clause (MPO_Draft_20270902.pdf). Vanessa — can you weighs in on the pricing/approval gating and legal risk for the 24-month flat commit?

If agreeable, we’ll prepare the AWS Private Offer, a DocuSign envelope, and a HubSpot deal update. I can also propose a one-time onboarding credit to help bridge the price/commit decision.

Best,
Olga
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: MPO_Draft_20270902.pdf]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jason Lewis <jason.lewis@brookline.ai>; Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 09:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace private offer — buyer approvals & term structure

Jason / Olga — quick note from Sales Ops / Legal viewpoint:

- Two-year flat commits: Legal flags pre-paid or fixed 24-month fees for usage-based products as potentially problematic if actual consumption is highly variable. If Brookline is comfortable with that risk, we can price accordingly, but contract will require explicit credits/true-ups for significant overage/underage.
- Suggested commercial structure that balances your needs: 12-month firm commitment + an optional second 12-month extension (at a negotiated discount) exercisable by procurement in Q4 of year 1. This keeps buyer signature to procurement and limits legal exposure.
- Approval sequencing: We can prepare the MPO with procurement as signer and include an "internal acceptance" attachment where BU heads confirm internal approval. That satisfies AWS MPO signing constraints and keeps the marketplace flow single-signer.

I’m attaching a short appendix with three pricing bands and suggested approval language (MPO_Terms_Options.pdf). Olga — pricing bands below are my recommendation for Brookline based on their expected annual run rate (you already included the ranges):
  - 12m firm commit: base price (0% discount baseline)
  - 12m + optional 12m: base - 8% on average
  - 24m upfront: base - 12% (requires legal credit/true-up clause)

I’ll also flag that multi-BU buyers sometimes prefer a pilot usage bucket under the MPO to reduce governance friction.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call to walk Jason through AWS MPO signer requirements if helpful.

—Vanessa
Sr. Sales Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: MPO_Terms_Options.pdf]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>; Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 10:30:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace private offer — buyer approvals & term structure

Team — thanks for the analysis. A few quick directives so we move fast and keep Brookline’s buying experience simple:  

1) Prioritize a single-signer MPO (procurement) with an internal approval memo from BU leads — we want to avoid multi-sign delays.  
2) Offer structure: present both: (A) 12m + optional 12m extension at -8% and (B) 24m upfront at -12%. Push for A as the default sales motion.  
3) To push the decision faster, offer a one-time onboarding credit ($25k) if Brookline signs the MPO within 10 business days.

Vanessa: greenlight the pricing bands you suggested. Olga: prepare the MPO and DocuSign envelope referencing the internal acceptance memo; coordinate with Aditya for any marketplace pricing record we need to set.

Vivek
VP, Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Jason Lewis <jason.lewis@brookline.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brookline.ai; Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 14:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace private offer — buyer approvals & term structure

Olga / Vanessa / Vivek — this all sounds reasonable and solves our internal friction. Procurement can sign on behalf of Brookline; we’ll attach a short internal approval memo from the BU leads.

Please proceed with option A (12m + optional 12m extension at -8%) and include the $25k onboarding credit in the DocuSign. Can you also:  
- Share the AWS private offer link and DocuSign when ready
- Add the PO template I attached to the DocuSign envelope so our finance team has it for records

We’re aiming to have the MPO signed by 2027-09-17. Thanks for moving quickly.

—Jason
Head of Procurement, Brookline AI
